h1:
Michelin Guide Phuket 2026
Eat the whole island, roadside to fine dining
intro: Phuket is the rare province where a few-baht plate of Roti Thaew Nam at breakfast and a table at Pru, its one-star Green Star kitchen, at dinner both make sense on the same day. In between sit real Southern Thai spots like One Chun and the always-queued braised pork at Go Benz.
quickAnswerHtml: Phuket has 20 Michelin 2026 restaurants — 1 star (Pru, which also holds a Green Star) and 19 Bib Gourmand.

faq.q: Which Phuket Michelin restaurant should I book ahead?
faq.a: Pru, the island's only one-star and a Green Star holder, is a set-menu fine-dining room starting around 7,200 baht, so reserve well ahead. Most of the Bib Gourmand spots are walk-in, though popular ones sell out, so go early.

faq.q: What is the cheapest Bib Gourmand in Phuket?
faq.a: Roti Chaofa starts at just 10–30 baht, and Khao Tom Dibuk and Pathongko Mae Pranee also land in the low tens. They make excellent, wallet-friendly breakfasts and snacks for Michelin-listed food.

faq.q: Where do I go for authentic Southern Thai food?
faq.a: Phuket is loaded with Southern Thai Bib Gourmand spots: One Chun, Kin-Kub-Ei, Krua Praya, Krua Baan Platong, Mor Mu Dong and Ton Mayom. Pick by neighborhood and expect bold, proper Phuket flavors.
Begin with Go Benz for its famous braised pork and rice congee, then add Roti Thaew Nam and One Chun in the old town. These three are easy to reach and cover the range of Phuket eating well.

faq.q: Are Phuket's Michelin restaurants spread far apart?
faq.a: Most cluster in Phuket Town and the old town, walkable or a short ride apart. A few like Toh Daeng sit in Thalang, so renting a car or booking rides lets you hit several in one day.
